paraphrase: Āśvalāyana approaches Parameṣṭhin for the highest knowledge of Brahman; he is told to know it by faith, devotion, meditation and yoga.

checks.note: E-text 1.1-2 located in the e-text; the passage matches the paraphrase.

paraphrase: Making the self the lower fire-stick and the praṇava the upper, by the churning of knowledge the wise burn the bond.

checks.note: E-text 1.11 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'ātmānamaraṇiṅkṛtvā praṇavaṃ cottarāraṇim | jñānanirmathanābhyāsātpāpaṃ dahati paṇḍitaḥ || 11…').

paraphrase: Deluded by māyā, the self in the body does everything in waking, enjoys in dream, and in deep sleep, overcome by darkness, attains happiness; from it arise the three worlds.

checks.note: E-text 1.12-14 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'sa eva māyāparimohitātmā śarīramāsthāya karoti sarvam | striyannapānādi-vicitrabhogaiḥ sa eva…').

paraphrase: 'That supreme Brahman, the self of all… that you are, you are that.'

checks.note: E-text 1.16 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'yatparaṃ brahma sarvātmā viśvasyāyatanaṃ mahat | sūkṣmātsūkṣmataraṃ nityantattvameva tvameva tat || 16…').

paraphrase: 'I am subtler than the subtle, greatest; I am the manifold universe; without hands and feet, of unthinkable power; I see without eyes, hear without ears; I am to be known by all the Vedas.'

checks.note: E-text 1.17-23 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyādiprapañcaṃ yatprakāśate | tadbrahmāha-miti jñātvā sarvabandhaiḥ pramucyate || 17 ||…').

paraphrase: Not by works, offspring or wealth; by renunciation alone some have reached immortality; beyond heaven, hidden in the cave, it shines, which the renouncers enter.

original.text: na karmaṇā na prajayā dhanena tyāgenaike amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ

paraphrase: Seated in solitude, pure, with head, neck and body straight, in the last stage of life, the renouncer meditates in the heart lotus on the Lord with Umā — three-eyed, blue-throated, tranquil.

checks.note: E-text 1.5-7 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'viviktadeśe casukhāsanasthaḥ śuciḥ samagrīvaśiraḥśarīraḥ | antyāśramasthaḥ sakalendriyāṇinirudhya bhaktyā…').

paraphrase: He is Brahmā, Śiva, Indra, the imperishable, the supreme, self-luminous; he is Viṣṇu, prāṇa, time, fire and moon; seeing oneself in all beings and all beings in oneself one reaches Brahman.

checks.note: E-text 1.8-10 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'sa brahmā sa śivaḥsendraḥ so'kṣaraḥ paramaḥ svarāṭ | sa eva viṣṇuḥ sa prāṇaḥ sa kālo'gniḥ sacandramāḥ || 8 ||…').

paraphrase: One who recites the Śatarudrīya is purified as by fire; he resorts to Avimukta; the one beyond the stages (atyāśramin) should recite it; by this knowledge he attains kaivalya.

checks.note: E-text khaṇḍa 2 is located: the Śatarudrīya, Avimukta, the atyāśramin, and kaivalya as the fruit.
